ChainLink 0.3.684

Make ChainLink yours: modules you can switch off, shareable bike builds, smarter training plans, and a faster app everywhere.

Modules — turn off what you don't use

Settings has a new Modules card. Every big area of ChainLink — Fitness Signature, Wellness, Routes, Events & Goals, Bikes & Workshop, Bike Fit, AI Coach, Weather, Reports — now has its own switch, plus one per connected service. Off means the pages, background work and coach input for that module stop on that device — your data stays saved and synced, and everything comes back exactly as it was when you switch it on again. Per-device on purpose: run your phone lean and your desktop fully loaded.

Share bike builds

Plan a build for a friend and send it to them: Share Build… on the build workbench saves a small file with every part, weight and price; Import Build… in the Bikes page's Add menu opens one. The recipient's shopping list starts fresh — nothing arrives pre-ticked as bought.

Smarter training plans

  • Public holidays, automatically. Generated plans know your region's holidays — a Monday holiday gets your best weekend time allocation without touching the availability grid. Your own entry for a date always wins.
  • Fitness tests that schedule themselves. Plans open with a short ramp test; later Build/Peak phases re-test with the two-effort CP protocol.
  • Honest completion. A planned session is only marked done by a ride that actually matches it — an easy spin no longer ticks off your FTP test, and tests only complete from a detected test effort or your own "Mark done" tick.
  • No more phantom workouts. The training calendar could show the same planned session several times on one day — leftovers from older plan generations now clean themselves up.

Pull to refresh — with feedback

Pull down on the Rides page (and others) to fetch new rides: a dotted line stretches as you pull and ripples while the sync runs. Also fixed a bug where the first pull could wrongly report your connected services as unreachable.

Faster everywhere

  • Your all-time power curve is now computed once by your strongest device and shared — on a phone it appears near-instantly instead of re-reading years of rides.
  • The Rides page no longer reads its whole history on the main thread, and two further speed bugs are fixed (huge unnecessary reads, and a full recompute on every launch). Older iPhones feel it most.
  • The header chart draws the current week, month and year full-width — the in-progress period used to be clipped to a sliver.

A note about Strava

As of 30 June 2026, Strava requires an active Strava subscription for the API access ChainLink's Strava connection uses. If your subscription has lapsed, the connection will stop working — that's Strava's change, not a ChainLink bug. Syncing through Garmin Connect is unaffected and remains the recommended way to get rides in.

ChainLink 0.3.682

Make ChainLink yours: modules you can switch on and off, shareable bike builds, and a snappier app all round.

Modules — turn off what you don't use

Settings has a new Modules card. Every big area of ChainLink — Fitness Signature, Wellness, Routes, Events & Goals, Bikes & Workshop, Bike Fit, AI Coach, Weather, Reports — now has its own switch, plus one per connected service (Strava, Ride with GPS, Garmin Connect, Karoo). Off means the pages, background work and coach input for that module stop on that device — your data stays saved and synced, and everything comes back exactly as it was when you switch it on again. Settings are per-device on purpose: run your phone lean and your desktop fully loaded.

Share bike builds

Plan a build for a friend and send it to them: the build workbench has a new Share Build… button that saves a small file with every part, weight and price, and the Bikes page's Add menu gained Import Build… to open one. The recipient's shopping list starts fresh — nothing arrives pre-ticked as bought.

Pull to refresh — now with feedback

  • Pull down on the Rides page (and any page with sync) to fetch new rides. A dotted line stretches as you pull and ripples while the sync runs.
  • Fixed a bug where the first pull could wrongly report your connected services as unreachable.

Faster, and more honest charts

  • Two real speed bugs fixed: ride pages no longer read hundreds of megabytes of graph data just to check it exists, and launch no longer recomputes your whole fitness history when nothing changed. Older iPhones feel it most.
  • The Rides header chart now draws the current week, month and year as a full-width bar — the in-progress period used to be clipped to a sliver, which made the Years view look like it ended last year.
  • The Goals, Wellness and Settings pages do far less repeated work while you scroll.

Training plan fixes

  • No more phantom workouts. The training calendar could show the same planned session several times on one day — leftovers from older plan generations. Duplicates and ghost plans now clean themselves up on launch.
  • Honest session completion. A planned session is only marked done by a ride that actually matches it (similar effort and length) — an easy spin no longer ticks off your FTP test. Tests only complete from a detected test effort or your own "Mark done" tick, and any session can still be marked done by hand from its detail sheet.

A note about Strava

As of 30 June 2026, Strava requires an active Strava subscription for the API access ChainLink's Strava connection uses. If your subscription has lapsed, the connection will stop working — that's Strava's change, not a ChainLink bug. Syncing through Garmin Connect is unaffected and remains the recommended way to get rides in.
